subject: physical-education
title: Reteach and varied practice: overhand throw mechanics
essentialQuestion: How do I send and receive an object accurately?
materials: unit equipment listed in the guardian safety review
movementCues: Throwing elbow high, hand back behind the head.
Step with the opposite foot, then rotate hips and shoulders through.
Follow through across the body towards the opposite hip.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Throwing front-on with the arm only, which is weak and inaccurate. Fix: start every throw from a side-on stance with the non-throwing arm pointing at the target.
keyPoints: Throwing elbow high, hand back behind the head.
Step with the opposite foot, then rotate hips and shoulders through.
Follow through across the body towards the opposite hip.
privacySafeScenario: Complete a personal throw-and-catch challenge at a distance you choose, and name which cue made your throw and your catch more controlled. Nothing is counted, timed, or recorded as a score.
studentTask: The learner practises overhand throw mechanics at a self-selected challenge level, using the adapted alternative whenever it fits better, and names the cue that helped.
knowledgeCheck: The learner names one cue that helped with overhand throw mechanics and one adjustment for next time, by demonstrating, describing, drawing, or writing.
completionCriteria: The learner takes part in the task about overhand throw mechanics at a self-selected challenge level.
The learner uses or names the movement cues for overhand throw mechanics.
The learner identifies one adjustment or next step. No score, time, count, or measurement is required.
adaptationChoices: Throwing, catching, and object control may use a larger, lighter, slower, or bounced object; a shorter distance; a rolled rather than thrown delivery; a scoop or two hands; or a stationary target. A learner may also direct a partner and analyze the result instead of performing the skill.
extensionChallenge: Apply overhand throw mechanics under one new condition of the learner choosing — different equipment, space, speed, or partner — and describe what changed.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show or describe a model before practice.
Allow demonstrated, described, drawn, spoken, signed, or written evidence; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-repetition, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-stimulation options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the movement target while adjusting equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, or support.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to enjoy one safe, optional activity that practises overhand throw mechanics. No purchase, account creation, recording, measurement, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
